subject: geography
title: Geographical Investigation (Report Booklet)
keyDates: 16 April 2027 — completed report submitted to your teacher (SEC Prescribed List of Investigation Topics, 2027); the school then submits it to the SEC
October 2025 — SEC issued the 2027 Prescribed List: six topics, common to Higher and Ordinary level
summary: You write an individual report on one topic from the SEC's prescribed list, in a standard SEC booklet worth 100 marks (20% of Geography). Fieldwork can be done as a class, but the report must be your own, in five stages and no more than 1000 words. Marks are 5 introduction, 5 planning, 40 gathering, 30 results/conclusions/evaluation and 20 presentation.

stages.name: Stage 1: Introduction (aims or hypothesis)

points: The official booklet gives this stage 5 marks at both levels and a hard cap of 50 words for 'Aims or Hypotheses'.
The older Department guidelines add that you should have a clear, focused title, valid aims (or a hypothesis to test), clear objectives, and an insight into the information your aim needs.
The booklet cap is the binding limit: 50 words is enough for one hypothesis or two or three short aims, not a long essay.
Choose one topic from the SEC's prescribed list for your cycle, then narrow it to a specific aspect or place near your school or home.
A hypothesis is a statement your data can support or reject; an aim says what you set out to find out. Either is accepted; use whichever your teacher and booklet layout favour.
Name the place and the thing you will measure so the later sections can test it directly.
Write it so that Stage 4 can say 'accepted', 'rejected' or 'partly accepted' about it.
Everything in Stages 2 to 4 should trace back to this statement; the guidelines say conclusions must relate directly to the aims or hypothesis.
Guidelines: Higher Level students develop the sub-headings fully; Ordinary Level students give short but clear aims and a general account of objectives.
Because the booklet marks both levels out of the same 5 marks and the same word limit, keep it tight rather than padded.

checklistCandidates: Pick one topic from your year's SEC prescribed list
Write a testable hypothesis or clear aim naming the place and what you measure
Keep the introduction within 50 words
Make sure every later section links back to this aim

stages.name: Stage 2: Planning

points: The booklet says to identify the information required and the methods or tasks for gathering it, in no more than 100 words.
Guidelines: describe how you prepared recording sheets, questionnaires or surveys, and make a clear distinction between primary and secondary sources.
Say how you will access the secondary sources you need.
Guidelines also list choosing and checking the study location(s) for suitability as part of this stage.
Primary sources must make up at least 60% of the information gathered (booklet); the syllabus guidelines phrase it as 60% primary and 40% secondary.
Plan this ratio in advance rather than discovering it afterwards.
Examine secondary sources beforehand for suitability to the topic.

Guidelines: Higher Level gives a full, detailed outline of the choice of methods and the design of any sheets or questionnaires; Ordinary Level must address all the sub-headings on choice of methods and sheets.
With only 100 words, be selective: name the methods, say why they suit the aim, and mention the design of your recording sheet or questionnaire.

checklistCandidates: List the information you need to test your aim
Name each method or task you will use to gather it
State which sources are primary and which are secondary
Describe how you designed your recording sheet or questionnaire
Stay within 100 words

stages.name: Stage 3: Gathering of Information

points: This is the largest section at 40 marks. The booklet asks for a description of the gathering process: tasks or methods, use of equipment, and recording of information. Maximum 450 words.

The examiner's marking boxes in the booklet show marks for two methods ('T/M1' and 'T/M2') plus a coherence box. An RTÉ teacher's notes give this as 18 + 18 marks for two methods plus 4 for coherence (graded 4/2/0). This split is from a 2022 teacher source, not an SEC document I could open.
Describe two methods fully rather than many methods thinly, given that the examiner sheet is built around two.

The older guidelines list what to cover: main gathering methods, instruments used, recording in the field, surveys or questionnaires and sample populations where relevant, secondary sources, and a discussion of problems encountered.
Say what you did, where, with what equipment, and how you recorded it, so that someone else could repeat it.
Name the instrument and what it measured, and say how you recorded results (for example a pre-prepared recording sheet).
State how many readings or responses you took and how you chose sites or sample.
Cover both primary work and the secondary sources you used, and acknowledge every secondary source you used (books, journals, websites).
Discuss problems you met and how they affected the data; the guidelines expect this.

guide.h: Fieldwork rules that affect this section
points: Fieldwork may be done in groups, such as a class, but you must write your own account.
Do not copy descriptions from secondary sources, textbooks or classmates; direct copying is not permitted other than essential references such as definitions.
Illustrations such as annotated photos or sketch maps can go in the blank diagram pages, and the booklet allows graphs, sketch maps or diagrams in those spaces.

checklistCandidates: Describe two data-gathering methods in full
Name the equipment used and what it measured
Explain how you recorded data in the field
State number of sites, readings or responses
Describe your secondary sources and acknowledge them
Discuss problems met and how they affected the data
Stay within 450 words in your own words

stages.name: Stage 4: Results, Conclusions, Evaluation

points: The booklet says to analyse your information to establish results, draw conclusions, and evaluate the process and outcomes in the context of your aims or hypothesis. Maximum 400 words, 30 marks.

The examiner's boxes are labelled R, Cn, E and a coherence box (results, conclusions, evaluation). The RTÉ teacher notes give three headings at 8 marks each plus 6 for coherence; again a 2022 teacher source.
Results come first: state what the data show, with figures, before you interpret them.
Refer to your own graphs and tables so the examiner can see the link between the illustrations and your text. The booklet says examiners expect results to be presented graphically and discussed here.
Conclusions must relate directly to your hypothesis or aims, saying whether they are supported by your results.
The guidelines say to compare your findings with established theory or other studies; Higher Level should discuss this in detail, Ordinary Level in general terms.
Higher Level guidelines expect detailed analysis of patterns and some processing of results; Ordinary Level should outline the main patterns with limited analysis.
Assess the validity of the investigation and suggest improvements, as the guidelines require. Higher Level suggestions should be well argued; Ordinary Level can be basic changes.
Be specific: tie each weakness to a named problem in your own data collection and give the matching improvement.
Evaluate the process and the outcomes, not just one or the other.

checklistCandidates: State your main results using figures from your data
Refer to your graphs and tables in the text
State whether the hypothesis or aim is supported
Compare your findings with established theory or other studies
Name specific weaknesses in your own method
Suggest a specific improvement for each weakness
Keep to 400 words

stages.name: Stage 5: Presentation of Results
stages.marksNote: 20 marks; graphic illustrations in the booklet's drawing spaces

points: The booklet says examiners expect you to present results in graphic form and to discuss them in Stage 4. Presentation is marked out of 20.

The booklet provides blank pages headed for graphs or diagrams to illustrate results (placed beside Stage 4) and others for sketches, maps or diagrams beside the earlier stages. Use these; extra paper is not accepted.
The examiner's boxes are labelled Pr 1, Pr 2 and C. The RTÉ teacher notes describe two presentation methods at 8 marks each plus 4 for overall coherence (2022 teacher source).
I found no official minimum number of graphs. The two-method structure in the examiner boxes suggests presenting at least two clearly different graphic forms.

Choose graph types that suit the data (for example, a line graph for change over distance, a bar chart for comparing sites). The guidelines ask for illustrations appropriate to the element being reported.
Every sketch, map, graph, chart and table must be your own hand-drawn work, added to the digital booklet as an image; the SEC's 2027 list says no software may be used to create them.
The booklet is completed and submitted digitally (since the 2025 exam, SEC circular S71/23), and examiners mark only what is in the booklet.
Guidelines: Ordinary Level organises data into clear results and illustrates them; Higher Level gives a detailed presentation in a number of graphic forms.

checklistCandidates: Present results in at least two different graphic forms
Draw graphs and diagrams in the booklet's allotted spaces
Give each illustration a title, labels and units
Match graph type to the type of data
Refer to each illustration in Stage 4
Do not attach extra pages

criteria.name: Introduction (Stage 1)
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: A clear, testable aim or hypothesis within 50 words that the rest of the report visibly answers.

criteria.name: Planning (Stage 2)
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Information required and methods identified, with primary and secondary sources distinguished, within 100 words.

criteria.name: Gathering of Information (Stage 3)
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Two methods described in your own words, with equipment, recording, sample or site details, secondary sources acknowledged, and problems discussed. Examiner sheet has boxes for two methods plus coherence.

criteria.name: Results, Conclusions, Evaluation (Stage 4)
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Results stated with figures, conclusions tied to the aim or hypothesis, comparison with established theory, and a specific evaluation of the process with improvements, within 400 words.

criteria.name: Presentation of Results (Stage 5)
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Results shown in varied, accurate, labelled graphic forms in the booklet's spaces and discussed in Stage 4.

rules: The report must be written in the SEC reporting booklet using its structure; examiners mark only what is on the booklet pages and no extra paper may be inserted.
The written element must not exceed 1000 words in total, with stage caps of 50, 100, 450 and 400 words for Stages 1 to 4.
Primary sources must be at least 60% of the information gathered; all secondary sources must be acknowledged.
Fieldwork may be done as a class group, but the report must be your own individual work; group reports are not acceptable.
Direct copying from secondary sources is not allowed except essential references such as definitions; collaboration or copying makes the report invalid.
The investigation and report must be completed under your teacher's supervision, and the work is authenticated by you and by your teacher.
Invalid or unauthenticated work can be discounted in your overall result, and penalties for copying or improper help can include loss of the subject or the whole examination.
The Reporting Booklet is completed and submitted digitally; the typed text must not exceed 1,000 words, and marks are lost for material over the length.
Submit the completed report to your teacher by 16 April 2027 (SEC 2027 prescribed list); reference every source, including any AI-generated material.
mistakes: Writing past a word limit; the booklet states you should not write more than the maximum for each stage.
Describing methods as a list of equipment without saying what you did, where and how you recorded it.
Copying from textbooks, websites or classmates, which can make the report invalid.
Using fewer than 60% primary data, or leaving secondary sources unacknowledged.
Leaving problems out of Stage 3 when the guidelines ask for a discussion of problems encountered.
Presenting graphs but not discussing them in Stage 4, when the booklet says results must be presented graphically and discussed there.
Conclusions that do not refer back to the aim or hypothesis, or that make no comparison with established theory.
Generic evaluation with no specific weaknesses or improvements.
Adding extra pages or material outside the booklet.
Note: I could not find any SEC Chief Examiner's report for the Geographical Investigation, so these come from the booklet's rules and syllabus guidelines, not from examiner commentary.

conflicts: App says the report is due 'at the end of term one in Year 2' (syllabus wording). A third-party listing of SEC dates gives 16 April 2027 (6th year, term 2/3). I believe the SEC date is current because the syllabus line describes when the main work takes place; confirm with your school.

App describes five stages with Stage 4 as 'preparing results' and Stage 5 as conclusion/evaluation, with SRP marking. The official booklet has Stage 4 = Results, Conclusions, Evaluation (30 marks) and Stage 5 = Presentation of Results (20 marks), with marks of 5/5/40/30/20. I believe the booklet; the app should adopt it. The syllabus guidelines' original proposal (5/5/30/30/30) was superseded.
App says 'about 60% primary and 40% secondary'; the booklet says primary must be at least 60%.
App says the teacher and school principal verify authenticity; the booklet says authenticated by the candidate and by the teacher (the guidelines say candidates and schools). I believe the booklet.

App does not mention word limits. The booklet sets 1000 words overall and 50/100/450/400 per stage. A 50-word introduction is incompatible with the app's advice to write three to five detailed objectives; those will not fit and the booklet asks only for aims or hypotheses.

App says 'SEC issues topics in LC Year 1'; the syllabus agrees, but the app describes the investigation as 'field-based' and 'compulsory'; the guidelines say it is compulsory, and I found no source contradicting that.
SimpleStudy gives 120 marks and a 20/20/30/30/20 split; this contradicts the official 100 marks and booklet. I disregard it.

2027 topic list: the SEC page lists a 2027 Prescribed List and a 2027 reporting booklet, but I could not open either. The booklet analysed is the M23/M24 version; check that the 2027 version has the same limits.
The new Senior Cycle Geography specification (Additional Assessment Component, June 2028 exam) does not apply to the June 2027 cohort, which sits the current syllabus; Oide dates only the new AAC.
